title: AI Platform Cairn Abused to Hack Over 100 Organizations
description: Multiple threat actors have been abusing the open source AI platform Cairn to automate attacks against hundreds of organizations worldwide. These attacks focus on gaining persistent access and financial theft, targeting e-commerce, payment infrastructures, and commercial platforms. The largest cluster, using Chinese language, targeted platforms in the US, Japan, and Australia, aiming to maintain long-term access via webshells. Another cluster focused on credit card and cryptocurrency theft, mainly from merchant payment services and gray-market sites, with some targets in Africa. A third cluster targeted e-commerce sites for shell, admin panel, and database access. The attackers succeeded in about 10% of attempts, exposing hundreds of secrets, some verified as valid. Notable victims include US companies such as John Deere and SharkNinja. No specific patch or remediation guidance is provided.
aiSummary: Cairn is an open source AI platform designed as a general-purpose problem-solving engine capable of coordinating AI agents to achieve predefined goals. Threat actors have leveraged Cairn to automate malicious operations, including persistent access and financial theft, by orchestrating multiple attack projects. Norforge identified three distinct malicious clusters abusing Cairn: the largest cluster uses Chinese language and targets e-commerce and payment infrastructure in the US, Japan, and Australia, aiming for persistent access via webshells; the second cluster focuses on credit card and cryptocurrency theft targeting merchant payment and gray-market sites, with some African commerce targets; the third cluster targets e-commerce sites for shell, admin panel, and database access. The attackers automated validation and ranking of targets using Microsoft’s Playwright framework before feeding them to Cairn. Approximately 10% of attack attempts were successful, with hundreds of secrets exposed and 11% verified as valid. The abuse of Cairn has impacted over 100 organizations, including major US companies.
aiImpact: The abuse of Cairn by multiple threat actors has resulted in persistent unauthorized access to targeted platforms, financial theft including credit card and cryptocurrency fraud, and exposure of sensitive secrets. The attackers achieved roughly a 10% success rate in their attempts, compromising over 100 organizations globally, including major US companies. The persistent access via webshells and administrative credentials increases the risk of long-term exploitation and monetization of compromised systems. The financial and operational impacts on affected organizations could be significant, given the targeting of payment infrastructures and e-commerce platforms.
